title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: During account registration, the Homeowner provides identified personal data (name, email, contact information) which is processed by the Home Hub. This creates a direct link between the data subject and their personal information.
assumptions: Registration requires personal identification information

title: Unique identifiers in device enrollment
description: Camera and sensor enrollment involves unique device identifiers that can be linked back to the Homeowner's account, creating persistent identification references.
assumptions: Devices have unique identifiers that are registered to the account

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The Home Hub can link all enrolled devices and account data through unique identifiers (account ID, device serial numbers), enabling comprehensive data association across the system.
assumptions: System uses unique identifiers for account and device management

title: Profiling through device enrollment patterns
description: The combination of account data and enrolled device types/locations can be analyzed to create profiles about the Homeowner's lifestyle, security preferences, and home layout.
assumptions: Device enrollment data includes location and type information

title: Potentially excessive data sensitivity in registration
description: Account registration may collect more sensitive personal data than functionally required for basic device enrollment (e.g., full name, address, phone number when only email might suffice).
assumptions: Registration form collects multiple personal data fields

title: Data retention beyond functional need
description: Registration and enrollment data may be retained longer than necessary for the functional purpose of device management, especially if account deletion or data purging policies are not clearly defined.
assumptions: System retains registration data indefinitely or for extended periods

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected during registration and device enrollment, including metadata, device identifiers, and how this data will be used.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not comprehensively explain all data processing activities

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Homeowner may lack granular control over which personal data is collected and how it is processed during registration and device enrollment.
assumptions: Registration process may not offer opt-out options for non-essential data collection

title: Attributable registration data
description: Registration and enrollment actions create data records that can be attributed to the specific Homeowner, preventing them from denying these account creation and device enrollment actions.
assumptions: System logs and stores registration/enrollment events with user attribution

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If the registration process collects more personal data than necessary for device enrollment functionality, this could violate GDPR's data minimization principle.
assumptions: Registration may collect data beyond functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices

title: Sensitive motion data collected
description: Motion alerts reveal presence/absence patterns at home, which is sensitive personal data that could expose when individuals are home or away.
assumptions: Motion data is considered sensitive as it reveals occupancy patterns

title: Fine-grained motion data disclosure
description: Real-time motion alerts provide highly granular data about movement patterns, more detailed than may be functionally necessary for basic alerting.
assumptions: Real-time alerts contain detailed motion information

title: High frequency data processing
description: Real-time motion alerts are processed continuously, creating high-frequency personal data processing that may exceed functional needs.
assumptions: Motion alerts are sent in real-time as motion is detected

title: Identifier in motion alert
description: Motion alerts likely contain device IDs, user IDs, or home identifiers that can uniquely identify the data subject.
assumptions: Alerts include identifying information to route to correct user

title: Revealing attributes in motion data
description: Motion patterns can reveal revealing attributes about data subjects such as daily routines, presence at home, and activity levels.
assumptions: Motion data contains patterns that reveal personal information

title: Profiling through motion patterns
description: Motion data can be analyzed to profile individuals' behavior patterns, daily routines, and presence at home over time.
assumptions: Motion data is stored and analyzed for patterns

title: Unawareness of motion tracking
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their motion is being tracked and transmitted to the mobile app backend in real-time.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of motion data collection

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Users may lack control to customize how motion data is collected, processed, or transmitted, including frequency and granularity settings.
assumptions: Limited user controls for motion data processing

title: Data minimization violation
description: Real-time motion alerts may process more personal data than functionally necessary, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Real-time granularity may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific functional requirements of the system

title: Motion data as attributable evidence
description: Motion alerts can serve as evidence that someone was present at a location at a specific time, preventing individuals from denying their presence.
assumptions: Motion alerts are timestamped and stored

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications sent to the homeowner can be analyzed to infer patterns about when the homeowner is present or absent from their property, enabling profiling of their daily routines and habits.
assumptions: The backend retains or processes motion detection data that could be analyzed for patterns over time.

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes identified data to route motion detection notifications to the specific homeowner's device, requiring identification of the data subject.
assumptions: The system uses homeowner identifiers to deliver notifications to the correct device.

title: Sensitive motion detection data disclosure
description: Motion detection notifications reveal sensitive information about property occupancy patterns, which could be considered highly sensitive personal data that should only be disclosed when strictly necessary.
assumptions: Motion detection data reveals when the homeowner is present or absent from their property.

title: Excessive notification frequency
description: If motion detection notifications are sent more frequently than functionally needed (e.g., for every minor motion event rather than significant security events), this could constitute excessive processing of personal data.
assumptions: The system may send notifications for all motion events without filtering for significance.
uncertainty_note: Depends on system configuration and notification filtering logic.

title: Lack of homeowner control over notification preferences
description: The homeowner may lack control over how motion detection notifications are processed, including preferences for frequency, timing, or types of motion events that trigger notifications.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular control options for notification preferences.
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether the app provides notification preference settings.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If motion detection notifications include more data than necessary (e.g., exact timestamps, location details, or motion intensity) beyond what is needed to alert the homeowner, this could violate GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: The notification may contain more detailed information than strictly required for the alert function.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual content of the notification payload.

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Device-usage analytics are shared with a cloud analytics vendor (EE3), a predetermined external party. This exposes personal data to a third party beyond the original system boundary, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor is a known, fixed party in the system architecture.

title: Data propagation to external service
description: Analytics data is propagated to an external cloud analytics vendor where it may be processed further, potentially beyond what is functionally necessary for the mobile app's core functionality.
assumptions: The analytics vendor may use the data for purposes beyond what the mobile app requires.

title: Quasi-identifier linking through aggregated analytics
description: Even aggregated device-usage analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., device type, usage patterns, time patterns) that could be combined with other data to identify individual users.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics may retain enough granularity to serve as quasi-identifiers when combined with external datasets.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual aggregation level and what attributes are included in the analytics.

title: Profiling through device usage patterns
description: Device-usage analytics can be analyzed to create profiles of individual users based on their usage patterns, behavior, and preferences, enabling linking of data to specific individuals.
assumptions: The analytics vendor has capability to perform profiling analysis on the received data.

title: User unawareness of analytics data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being collected and shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, especially if this is not clearly disclosed in privacy notices.
assumptions: Privacy disclosures may not clearly explain third-party analytics sharing.

title: Lack of user control over analytics processing
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are processed and shared with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: The mobile app may not provide granular consent options for analytics sharing.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external vendor may violate GDPR's data minimization principle if more data is shared than is strictly necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: The analytics sharing may include data beyond what is functionally required.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific data elements included in the analytics and the stated purpose.

title: Potential invalid consent for analytics sharing
description: If users have not provided valid, informed consent for sharing device-usage analytics with the cloud analytics vendor, this constitutes unlawful processing under GDPR.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not be properly implemented or may be bundled with other terms.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the actual consent implementation in the mobile app.

title: Sensitive video data stored
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage contain highly sensitive personal data including visual recordings of the homeowner's property and potentially people, which may be more sensitive than functionally required for playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content includes personal data of homeowners and potentially other individuals

title: Extended video retention
description: Video clips may be stored longer than functionally needed for the playback feature, creating unnecessary privacy risk through prolonged data retention.
assumptions: Storage duration is not explicitly limited to playback needs

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The mobile app backend processes video clips that are associated with identified homeowners, as the system must know which homeowner's video to retrieve for playback.
assumptions: Video storage is organized by homeowner account/identity

title: Revealing attributes in video content
description: Video content itself may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject, such as facial features, property characteristics, or other identifying visual information.
assumptions: Video content includes visual information that could identify individuals

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: Video files or their metadata likely contain unique identifiers (user IDs, account IDs, timestamps) that can link the video data to specific homeowners.
assumptions: Video storage system uses identifiers to organize and retrieve homeowner videos

title: Limited control over video deletion
description: Homeowners may lack adequate control to rectify or erase their video data, particularly if retention policies are not transparent or deletion mechanisms are not user-accessible.
assumptions: Video deletion requires backend intervention or has unclear user controls
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about actual user control mechanisms

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Storing and retrieving full video clips may process more personal data than actually needed for the playback functionality, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Full video clips are retrieved rather than minimal necessary data
